structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E058.

**Tip (E049, 3df6233).** 237 steps at batch 2000. Resolution is 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30% of steps. The whitening bias is detached at 20%, the stem frozen at 75%, and group 2 annealed from 75% and frozen at 90%. Seeds 0–2 across four builds: 0.7535, 0.7552, 0.7536, 0.7522 (E058's rebuild context). Time is 5.20–5.22 s. Unselected population mean is about 0.7528 ±0.01, so there is about 0.25–0.3 pp over the 0.75 bar before judge and rebuild drift.

**Noise.**
- Per-seed SD is about 0.3 pp, so a 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp.
- The build spread on seeds 0–2 (0.30 pp across E049/E050/E057/E058-era builds) is consistent with seed noise plus a small build term. I take σ_build ≈ 0.05–0.12 pp for a 20-seed mean.
- Time reproduces to about 1%.

**E058.** Re-building E052/E053 read 0.7522 at 5.00 s. Both sit at the gate margin and were discarded, as I predicted. Faster candidates around 0.752 keep failing the 0.753 3-seed test about half the time. That is the structural problem: the gate costs about 0.2 pp of margin, which is worth about 0.3 s at the dial rate.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ(steps × per-step cost).
- Per-step cost: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s.
- The stem freeze saves 0.0087 s/step and the group-2 freeze about 0.010 s more.
- Correction from my misses: removals (E052 selection, E056 ReLU) came in 2–4% faster than the MAC model. I now apply −3% to the modelled time of any removal.
- The whitening detach moving 20% → 6% saves only g1.conv1 dgrad and whitening backward at 20 px (about 33 steps × 1–2 ms ≈ 0.04–0.06 s, roughly 1%), which is within rebuild time noise.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost).**

| Lever | Rate / status |
|---|---|
| Epoch dial | ~0.8–1.5 |
| ReLU | ~1 |
| Width | ~0.7 |
| Stride instead of pool | ~0.45 |
| Data selection | about the dial |
| Group-2 freeze at 90% | near free |
| Group-2 freeze at 85% | worse |
| Stem freeze at 75% | optimal; 71% and 60% are worse |

**Mechanisms.**
1. Accuracy is bought with steps on layers that are still learning (E041, E045, E053, E054, E055).
2. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is tuned (E025, E030).
3. The late 28/32 px phases carry accuracy. Early phases are step-limited, not pixel-limited (E026, E033 free; E040, E041 cost).
4. Muon renormalizes filters every step, so filter wd is inert.
5. BN scale is already frozen (`BatchNorm.__init__`), so I092 closes by code read.
6. The harness supplies fine labels only, so I091 is blocked: a hard-coded mapping would be external data.
7. Under Muon, ||ΔW||/||W|| redraws the imposed LR schedule, so I094's curves can't separate E028 from E037.

**Strategy.** The remaining time headroom is small: each idea moves time by about 1–3%, which is about the size of build noise. The best expected value is near-free truncations (whitening detach at 6%) stacked with careful gate accounting, not more dose sweeps. E046 at 5.08 s is the obvious gate candidate, but its population mean is about 0.752, so it probably fails one of the two confirmation tests.

**Unsure.**
- The size of σ_build.
- Winner's curse vs seed-set difficulty.
- How much drift the PCIe judge adds.
- Whether the whitening bias really finishes learning by 6% under this schedule.

forecasts.reason: E046 rebuild. A 6-step difference gives about 0.1 pp, which is below σ_tot for a 20-seed paired difference that includes build noise. The dial rate stays undetermined between 0.7 and 1.5 s/pp.
The harness supplies only fine labels, and a hard-coded coarse map is external data. This should be blocked with no run; any measurement would just be a tip rebuild.
BatchNorm.__init__ already sets weight.requires_grad=False, so this closes by code read. Any run is a tip rebuild.

It saves only about 33 cheap-phase steps × 1–2 ms (about 0.05 s, roughly 1%), which is within build time noise. The accuracy effect should be under 0.1 pp and unresolvable. The time part may be supported by CUDA-event timing.
Muon's fixed-norm, orthogonalized updates make ||ΔW||/||W|| track lr_t, so the curves just redraw the annealing schedule. They won't separate E028 (free) from E037/E055 (costly).

cruxes: What is σ_build for a 20-seed mean? If it is ≥0.1 pp, every sub-0.15 pp keep decision is noise, and the only reliable time wins are those with zero accuracy cost.

What is the true post-freeze dial rate (E046 vs E049 on the same fresh seeds)? Below 1 s/pp, trimming epochs beats every remaining structural lever; above 1.5 s/pp, near-free truncations such as the 6% whitening detach dominate.
Is the tip's unselected population mean ≥0.753 or ~0.752? That decides whether any time-cutting candidate can pass the 3-seed ≥0.753 gate more than half the time.
